prompt: Customers earn points automatically on orders and receive automatic discounts at checkout when points reach a configurable threshold.

intent.desiredOutcome: Customers earn points automatically on orders and receive automatic discounts at checkout when points reach a configurable threshold.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version handles the order webhook to award points accurately, stores balances durably per customer, and applies discounts correctly at checkout without double-applying or losing points. Edge cases: guests at checkout (no points), simultaneous orders affecting balance, ensuring discount math is clear. Admin UX should make threshold and earning rate obvious and easy to change. Avoid complexity — keep it one earning rule and one redemption rule.

plan.dataFlow: When a paid order event arrives, the system checks whether a points transaction already exists for that order; if so, it exits as a no-op. Otherwise it computes points earned using the configured earning rate, appends a credit transaction to the ledger, and increments the customer's running balance. If the updated balance meets or exceeds the configured redemption threshold, the system debits the threshold amount from the balance, appends a debit transaction, and creates a single-use discount code in Shopify, recording the grant against the customer. On the storefront, the widget reads the customer's current points balance and any active unredeemed discount code so the customer can see their standing and copy their code at checkout. The merchant adjusts the earning rate and redemption threshold from the admin settings page, with changes taking effect on all subsequent orders.

triggers.idempotency: if a points transaction row already exists for the order external id, treat the event as a no-op and perform no balance update or discount generation

capabilities.description: Calculate how many points a customer earns for a paid order by multiplying the order subtotal by the configured earning rate.
Append a credit transaction to the ledger and atomically increment the customer's running balance by the earned points amount.
Determine whether a customer's updated balance meets or exceeds the configured redemption threshold.
Create a single-use discount code in the external platform for the customer's earned discount value.
Append a debit transaction and write the discount grant record, linking the generated code to the customer and the points redeemed.
Read a customer's current points balance and most recent active discount grant for display in the storefront widget.
Read the current earning rate, redemption threshold, and discount value from the program settings record.
Persist an updated earning rate, redemption threshold, and discount value supplied by the merchant from the admin panel.
Return a paginated list of all customer point balances for the merchant admin overview.

persistence.name: program_settings
persistence.purpose: Stores the single merchant-configurable loyalty program configuration: earning rate, redemption threshold, and discount value.

columns.name: earning_rate
columns.purpose: points awarded per whole currency unit spent

columns.name: redemption_threshold
columns.purpose: minimum points balance required to generate a discount code

columns.name: discount_value
columns.purpose: monetary value of the discount code generated at redemption

persistence.keyedBy: single row representing the only program configuration record
queryPatterns: single row fetch for the current configuration on every order event and storefront request

persistence.name: customer_point_balances
persistence.purpose: Maintains the authoritative running points balance for each customer to support fast reads on the storefront widget and threshold checks.

columns.name: customer_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the customer whose balance this row represents

persistence.keyedBy: one row per customer, deduplicated by customer external id
queryPatterns: single row lookup by customer external id for balance reads and atomic increment or decrement
all rows ordered by points balance descending for the admin customer list

persistence.name: point_transactions
persistence.purpose: Immutable ledger of every points credit and debit event per customer, enabling auditing and idempotency checks.

columns.name: customer_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the customer whose balance is affected

columns.name: order_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the paid order that caused a credit transaction; null for debit transactions

columns.name: transaction_kind
columns.purpose: credit for points earned, debit for points redeemed against a discount grant

persistence.keyedBy: one credit row per paid order per customer, deduplicated by order external id; debit rows are keyed by the associated discount grant
queryPatterns: existence check by order external id to enforce idempotency before awarding points
all transactions for a given customer ordered by creation time for audit

persistence.name: discount_grants
persistence.purpose: Tracks every discount code generated for a customer when their points balance crosses the redemption threshold, including whether it has been used.

columns.name: customer_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the customer the discount code belongs to

columns.name: discount_code_external_id
columns.purpose: identifies the discount code record in the external platform; null until successfully created

columns.name: discount_code_value
columns.purpose: human-readable code string the customer enters at checkout

persistence.keyedBy: one row per discount generation event per customer
queryPatterns: most recent active (unredeemed) discount grant for a given customer for storefront display
all grants for a given customer ordered by creation time for audit

externalContracts.purpose: Return the current earning rate and redemption threshold so the merchant can review the program configuration.
Save a new earning rate, redemption threshold, and discount value for the loyalty program.
Return a paginated list of customers with their current points balances for merchant oversight.
Return the authenticated customer's current points balance and any active unredeemed discount code so the widget can render the correct state on page load.

edgeCases: Duplicate order-paid event delivery for the same order — the idempotency check on point transactions must exit before any balance mutation or discount evaluation occurs.

Duplicate order-paid event arrives after a partial processing failure (credit recorded but discount generation incomplete) — the idempotency check must distinguish a fully-committed processing record from a partially-committed one, e.g. by checking both the point transaction row and the resulting discount_grants row before deciding no-op vs. resumption.

Two paid orders for the same customer arrive near-simultaneously — the balance increment and threshold check must execute atomically to ensure at most one discount code is generated per threshold crossing.
Guest checkout with no associated customer record — skip all points processing and do not create any ledger or balance row.

External platform rejects discount code creation after points have already been debited — the debit transaction and balance decrement must be rolled back so the customer does not lose points without receiving a code.

Shopify discount code creation succeeds but the local record-discount-grant write fails before commit — on retry, the system must detect the already-created Shopify code (by idempotency key or lookup) and skip re-creation, then re-attempt only the local write.

Merchant lowers the redemption threshold after customers have already accumulated points — the new threshold applies only on the next order event; no retroactive discount codes are generated for customers who already meet it.
Customer has an active unredeemed discount code when a new threshold crossing occurs — do not generate a second code; wait until the existing grant is used or expires before issuing a new one.

hld_v_findings.issue: X3: The widget GET route '/widget/points/status' declares `"customer_external_id": "identifier"` in its requestShape, but the widget cannot securely supply this value — it is a server-side identity that must be resolved from the authenticated session, not passed in by the caller. A caller-supplied customer_external_id opens a horizontal privilege-escalation path where one customer can query another's balance and discount code simply by changing the parameter.
hld_v_findings.fix: Remove 'customer_external_id' from the requestShape of GET /widget/points/status; the LLD should resolve the customer identity from the authenticated session context, not from a caller-supplied field.

hld_v_findings.issue: C2: The 'generate-discount-code' capability calls out to the Shopify Admin API to create a discount code but there is no paired write capability and no edge case that records the outcome when the Shopify call succeeds but the subsequent 'record-discount-grant' DB write fails. The edge case present covers the rollback direction (Shopify rejects → roll back debit) but not the opposite split-brain: Shopify accepts → app crashes before persisting the grant → the code exists in Shopify but the customer never sees it and a retry will generate a second code.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case explicitly covering 'Shopify discount code creation succeeds but the local record-discount-grant write fails before commit — on retry, the system must detect the already-created Shopify code (by idempotency key or lookup) and skip re-creation, then re-attempt only the local write.'

hld_v_findings.issue: C5: 'record-discount-grant' has `"usesWorkflow": true`, but the discount_grants table's statusField is null and there is no stateMachine — meaning there is no declared lifecycle for this capability to own. The 'status' column on discount_grants represents an application workflow (pending → active → used/expired), and the spec reserves usesWorkflow=true for capabilities that own and write status transitions on a declared lifecycle. A capability that merely inserts the initial row (with an initial status) and never transitions it should be usesWorkflow=false; if a separate transition capability (e.g. mark-discount-used) is intended, it is missing from the plan.
hld_v_findings.fix: Either set usesWorkflow=false on 'record-discount-grant' (it performs an initial-state insert only) and add a separate capability that transitions discount_grants.status when the code is used or expires, OR confirm the insert-only intent and set usesWorkflow=false with no further change.

hld_v_findings.issue: T1: The external-event trigger for 'an order is paid' includes idempotency text on the trigger itself, but the edgeCases list addresses only the duplicate-delivery scenario for the balance/discount path. There is no edge case covering a duplicate delivery that arrives *after* a partial failure — e.g. the first delivery credited points but crashed before the debit/discount step; the second delivery finds a transaction row for the order and exits as a no-op, silently leaving the customer with a balance that should have triggered a discount. The deduplication anchor exits unconditionally on any existing transaction row, which conflates 'fully processed' with 'partially processed'.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add an edge case: 'Duplicate order-paid event arrives after a partial processing failure (credit recorded but discount generation incomplete) — the idempotency check must distinguish a fully-committed processing record from a partially-committed one, e.g. by checking both the point transaction row and the resulting discount_grants row before deciding no-op vs. resumption.'

hld_v_findings.issue: T2: The trigger's signalFields include `"order subtotal"` which is consumed by 'compute-points-earned', and `"customer external id"` which is consumed by 'record-points-credit' and 'get-customer-points-status'. However, the signal field `"order external id"` is listed on the trigger and is used by 'record-points-credit' and the idempotency check described in the dataFlow, yet no capability explicitly lists 'order external id' in dataNeeds for the idempotency guard step — the check is described only in the trigger's idempotency prose and in the edgeCases, leaving the LLD without a capability anchor to generate the guard logic against.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add 'order external id' to the dataNeeds of 'record-points-credit' (it already writes it to point_transactions) and ensure the idempotency pre-check is expressed as a dataNeed on a dedicated read capability or on 'record-points-credit' itself so the LLD has an explicit anchor for the existence check query.
